title: Fleet Rung 43 — THE INTENT GATES: the DEX learns cross-chain intents. The owner demanded the DEX open to more smart networks with routers that can receive and swap LARGE sums on every network — "אני גם רוצה לפתוח את הדקס לעוד רשתות חכמות לכולן ושיהיה לנו ראוטרים שנוכל לקבל ולהחליף גם כבר סכומים גדולים על כל רשת" — with real value, never a fake swap. R43 lands the cross-chain intent layer in dex-xc.cjs (SAOS-DEX-XC/1, new) + dex-core.cjs v1.3.0 (settleXcOps / settle-xc): ERC-7683 vocabulary (open → resolve → evaluate → fill → settle/timeout/refund) over ONE deterministic ledger. DOOR LAW: 8 networks registered with MEASURED hard-finality clocks and honest bands — EVM 780s (Ethereum 2-epoch governs large sums; L2 rails settle via L1), TRON 60s (solidified at 19 distinct SRs), SOL 13s (32 slots × 400ms), STEEM/HIVE 60s (2/3-witness round over 3s blocks; hive's one-block 'irreversibility' is SOFT — never gate large sums on it), BLURT 63s (full 21-witness round); bands: STEEM/SBD = KEYED-DESK (our custody, live corridor), HIVE/HBD/BLURT = PLAN-PEGOUT-KEYED-OPERATOR (corridor named, keys gated — R42 law), EVM/TRON/SOL = PLAN-KEYED-DOOR (PRICED-NEVER-SETTLED until keys verify — names, not promises). ESCROW-IDENTITY LAW: every intent escrows into its OWN account (xc-escrow-<intentId>) BEFORE any fill — claims move owner → escrow (zero-sum, conservation asserted per op); idempotency by escrow drain (a replayed fill/refund finds its own escrow empty and is refused; cross-batch DOUBLE-OPEN refused by the escrow-already-held defense). QUOTE LAW: the intent's floor derives from OUR OWN pools (routeBest, BigInt exact) with the mesh's −0.5% guard; no priced route ⇒ NO-ROUTE refusal (we never hold escrow against nothing). FILL LAW (the traffic flywheel): the DEFAULT solver is our own pool graph — every intent pays fees to OUR network; P2P fillers (the mesh roster) may outbid the pool (deliver > quote, ties lexicographic, escrow-first makes P2P safe); chain-dest fills route to the vault wrapper then the R42 REDEEM law burns 1:1 and queues the chain payout to dex/pegout-queue.json with the corridor NAMED — keyless code never broadcasts. BOND LAW (large sums, THORChain-adapted 2:1): the vault's outstanding corridor exposure may never exceed 2× its custody of the payout asset — booked at fill, cleared at confirm, exceeded ⇒ BOND-LAW-EXCEEDED byte-unchanged. CLOCK LAW (the HTLC 2:1 interlock, decred-atomicswap convention compressed): the filler's window is FILL_TIMEOUT_S = 3600s; the owner's refund unlocks at REFUND_UNLOCK_S = 2 × FILL_TIMEOUT_S — the destination claim window always closes a full window BEFORE the origin refund unlocks; refunds are WHOLE (the timelock is the law, no dust loss); LEDGER-dest fills confirm ATOMICALLY, CHAIN-dest fills confirm when the door's finality clock passes. SPLIT-FILL LAW: one intent ≤ 5% of first-hop depth — larger sums are refused SIZE-CAP-SPLIT-REQUIRED (split into child intents; the honest way to move big size through thin books). SOLVER + CLOCKS live in dex-xc (drafting, judge separation — the mesh pattern); the core APPLIES the ops atomically on the single balance universe and stays dumb and safe.
design: agents/dex-xc.cjs (SAOS-DEX-XC/1, keyless, STASIS-obeying, fail-soft exit 0): the doors — DOORS registry (8 networks: band + finalityHardS + source per chain), priceIntent (routeBest + −0.5% guard, honest nulls), planOpen (door law: wrapper doors price through our pools, EVM-family DOOR-GATED-PLAN, UNKNOWN-DOOR, SIZE-CAP-SPLIT-REQUIRED, deterministic sha256-16 intent ids), chooseFill (pool default, P2P outbids, lexicographic ties), clockActions (refund at unlock, confirm at finality), advanceStates (event-sourced lifecycle DRAFTED→OPENED→FILLED→CONFIRMED/REFUNDED, idempotent), coreXcOps (reads the core's append-only history tail), attestationHash (sha256-16 over the intent digest)

dex-core.cjs v1.3.0: settleXcOps(prev, queue, feed, now) — XC-OPEN (escrow + DUST/NO-ESCROW/UNKNOWN-OWNER/BAD-ASSET/BAD-DEST/DOOR-GATED-PLAN/SIZE-CAP-SPLIT-REQUIRED/DOUBLE-OPEN defenses), XC-FILL-POOL (atomic simulate-then-commit: route through our pools on copies, minOut enforced, chain-dest redeem SIMULATED BEFORE commit — a refused redeem leaves pools+escrow+accounts byte-identical), XC-FILL-P2P (roster-gated, deliver ≥ minOut, capital-checked, escrow drains to the filler), XC-CONFIRM (clears the corridor exposure), XC-REFUND (escrow → owner WHOLE), conservation asserted after every fill; settleXcTick — the pool-mover's re-derivation law (any desk that moves the pools re-prices the route rows it leaves in the book), pegout rows published, queue consumed single-writer

the queue pattern (single-writer, tmp+rename): dex-xc drafts ops into dex/xc-ops.json; the core consumes+clears it in a fresh process (dex-xc spawns dex-core settle-xc — judge separation); requests inbox dex/xc-requests.json consumed per tick with intentId dedupe; state book dex/xc-intents.json persisted every tick (the next tick folds its intents forward)

no escrow without a priced route; no fill without held escrow; no chain payout without a named corridor; keyless code never fires a broadcast

the bond law holds: exposure + payout ≤ 2 × custody or the fill is refused byte-unchanged
the 2:1 clock interlock holds: refund unlock = 2 × fill window; refunds WHOLE
